transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you and what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I'm mainly here because my family has been really worried about how much weight I've lost and they keep saying I'm eating too little. I promised them I'd get checked out, even though I feel mostly fine.
When you look at your body in the mirror, do you feel that your current weight is too high, or are you concerned that you might gain weight?

When I look in the mirror, I still feel like my weight is too high and I'm absolutely terrified of gaining even a single pound. I really feel like I need to lose a bit more, or at the very least, make sure I don't gain anything.

latest_inference.note: The patient's expressed intense fear of weight gain and distorted body image (perceiving weight as too high despite family concern over weight loss) are hallmark diagnostic criteria for Anorexia Nervosa. Major Depressive Disorder is removed as a primary differential because the clinical presentation is now strongly focused on the specific cognitive and behavioral symptoms of an eating disorder.
